Senses.PreferredTarget: an at-ease person of the Way
AlternateTargets: an unoccupied person of the Way
an idle person of the Way
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "an idle or at-ease person of the Way" (閑道人). Chan usage bends ordinary idleness into a named epithet, most often in the full line "an at-ease person of the Way who has ended study and does nothing contrived" (絕學無為閑道人). Huangbo explains that people of old heard one statement and thereby "ended study" (絕學), and so received this name; he contrasts them with people seeking much knowledge and many explanations. Tianru explicitly lists "the great sea of extinction" (大寂滅海), "the ground of actual principle" (實際理地), and this full epithet as different names for "great rest" (大休). The Mirror Record distinguishes accumulating study, ending study, and then passing beyond both, saying that only on reaching the end of study does one first draw near the Way. Other records deploy the shortened term in verse: the whole world is full of people seeking buddha, but an at-ease person of the Way is hard to find (茫茫盡是覓佛漢，舉世難尋閑道人). The epithet therefore names a Chan roster type through explicit ending-study and great-rest definitions, not a generic loafer.
Senses.Note: The exact short form has 37 hits in 33 allowlisted texts. Its stable expansion is 'ended-study, doing-nothing-contrived, at-ease person of the Way.' Evidence includes explicit naming formulas, a list of synonyms, prose distinctions among kinds of study, and verse deployment. The ordinary reading 'idle person' alone misses the corpus-defined epithet.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人心利纔聞一言便乃絕學所以喚作絕學無為閑道人今時人只欲得多知多觧廣求文義
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄): Huangbo Xiyun is the continuing speaker in his named record and calls the old exemplar an idle person of the Way who has ended learning.

Occurrences.Kwic: 謂之大寂滅海，謂之實際理地，謂之絕學無為閑道人，皆大休之異名也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 天如惟則禪師語錄: complete-case exact-turn review identifies Tianru Weize as the actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如此一念萬年、萬年一念，猶太虛空，不與萬象森羅為礙，豈不名絕學無為閑道人也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Abridgment of the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guting (古庭禪師語錄輯略): in his Niushou daily record, Guting Shanjian says that one thought for ten thousand years and ten thousand years in one thought, unobstructed like empty space, is called the person of the Way beyond learning and contrivance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：茫茫盡是覓佛漢，舉世難尋閑道人。棒喝交馳成藥忌，了亡藥忌未天真。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 1–33 (五燈全書(第1卷-第33卷)): in his hall address, Pan'an Jicheng contrasts a world of buddha-seekers with the rarity of an at-ease person of the Way.

Occurrences.Kwic: 習學既盡。謂之絕學無為閑道人。及至絕學。方始與道相近。直得過此二學。是謂真過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). After citing Yongjia Xuanjue's wording, Yuanwu Keqin explains completed accumulated study, ended study, drawing near the Way, and passing beyond both kinds of study.
